settings.headline: We build websites that outlast the launch party
settings.subtitle: Halverline is a fictional, independent web design and development studio founded in 2016. We work with organizations that want to own their website: the code, the content and where it runs.

settings.headline: Ten years, sixty sites, eight people
settings.body:
Mara Halverson and Desmond Lyle started the studio after a decade of watching clients rebuild their websites every three years. Our sites are meant to be run by the client's own team for a long time.

See the team, the work and our services.

items.title: The client owns it
items.text: Code in the client's repository, data in the client's database, and a CMS with an open-source license. No lock-in by design.

items.title: Accessible by default
items.text: Every template is tested with a keyboard and a screen reader before launch, not after a complaint.

items.title: Fast and plain
items.text: Server-rendered pages, little JavaScript and images sized for phones. Most of our pages weigh under 400 KB.

items.title: Editors first
items.text: Content models that match how the client actually publishes, so editors do not fight the CMS.

items.title: No seat tax
items.text: We price per project and per care plan, never per editor or per site.

items.title: Write it down
items.text: Weekly written updates in the client portal, and handover docs on every project.

items.a: No. Halverline, its team, clients and case studies are fictional. Any resemblance to a real agency is accidental.
It is a Raytha use case: a full agency website with case studies and a members-only client portal, built on an open-source .NET CMS, with a kit you can rebuild yourself.

items.q: Where do the images come from?
items.a: Every logo, mockup, portrait and PDF was generated by a script, so nothing here shows a real company, website or person.
